Narrowed three overstated firsts: The Jazz Singer was not the first feature with sound (Don Juan, 1926, had a synchronised score) but the first with synchronised spoken dialogue; Psycho is regarded as the first American film to show a toilet being flushed, not the first to show a toilet at all; Gandhi's funeral crowd is 'over 300,000' per Guinness and 'nearly 300,000' per other counts, so 'around 300,000'. Body sentences and the milestone table changed in EN/DE/RU.

'First feature-length film with sound' is ambiguous (Don Juan, 1926, already had synchronised music and effects); narrowed to the first feature with synchronised spoken dialogue, which is what The Jazz Singer is credited with.
